chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who places all of his zakat among his own family (Ahl al-Bayt), and they are your relatives, so he said, 'Yes.'
As for if they are dissenters (or of a different sect), it is not permissible to give them [zakat], even if they are relatives; what indicates this is what has been narrated:

key_terms.مُخَالِفِينَ: dissenters / those of a different sect

ai.seo_question: Can a Shia Muslim give zakat to their non-Shia relatives?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that while zakat may be given to one's own family, the condition of religious alignment (*wilayah*) is paramount; thus, relatives who are *mukhalifin* (dissenters, often interpreted as Sunnis in Shia jurisprudence) are excluded. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of *Tawalli wa Tabarri* (loyalty and disavowal), linking financial charity to theological affiliation rather than mere kinship. The hadith highlights that zakat serves not only as economic relief but also as a means of strengthening the Shia community's internal cohesion.
